transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well... I guess I'm here because I just feel like I’m coming apart at the seams. 

It's, um, it's ever since these foreclosure notices started coming in the mail. I just can't seem to handle it. I've been sitting out in my truck crying before I even clock in for work. I jump every single time the phone rings. And it's really affecting my job, too. I've been snapping at the apprentices, and I'm making stupid mistakes out in the repair bay that I never, ever would’ve made before. I just... I don't know what to do anymore.
When did you first start experiencing these feelings of anxiety and distress — was it right around the time you received the first foreclosure notice, or had you been feeling this way before that?

No, I was doing fine before all this. I was functioning totally normally until the foreclosure letters and the bank calls started coming in. It was really just... I'd say within a few weeks of getting that first formal notice in the mail, that's when everything just started unraveling for me, both at the shop and at home. Before that, I wasn't feeling like this at all.

Since those foreclosure notices started coming in a few weeks ago, have you been feeling this anxious and distressed pretty much every day without letup, or has it come and gone — like some days are better than others?

It's been pretty much every day. Like I said, it started a few weeks after that first notice, and... well, it's been going on for about four months total now. Just a constant weight every single day since this whole mess with the bank started.

You mentioned it's been a constant weight every day for about four months now. But even on those days when you're feeling this way, have there been any periods — maybe a few hours or even a full day — where you felt noticeably better or the anxiety eased up, or has it truly been unrelenting without any breaks?

Honestly, I haven't really noticed any breaks like that. It just feels... well, it feels pretty unrelenting. I don't think there's been a full day, or even a few hours, where the weight of it really eases up. It's just always there.

You mentioned the anxiety feels unrelenting, but I want to clarify — in these past four months, have there been any days where you woke up and the anxiety or distress was noticeably lighter or less intense than on other days, even if it didn't completely go away?

No, not really. I mean... maybe some mornings I'm just so exhausted that I don't feel it the exact second I open my eyes, but as soon as I actually wake up and remember the house and the shop, it's right back to being just as heavy. So, no, I haven't noticed any days where it actually felt less intense.

Looking back over these four months since the foreclosure started, would you say the intensity of your anxiety and stress has gotten better, worse, or stayed pretty much the same as it was in those first few weeks?

Honestly, I'm not really sure if it's changed much. It... it feels like it's stayed pretty much exactly the same as when it first hit. I haven't noticed it getting any better, but I don't know that I'd say it's gotten worse, either. It's just been that same heavy feeling the whole time.

In these four months, have there been any times when you had a break from worrying about the house situation — like maybe a weekend away, or even just a few hours when you weren't thinking about it — and did the anxiety actually ease up during those times?

No, I haven't really had any breaks like that. I haven't taken a weekend away or anything. Even if I'm at work in the shop, under a truck, trying to focus on what I'm doing... it's still right there in the back of my mind. I don't think there's been a time where I wasn't thinking about it or where the anxiety let up.

During these four months, has there been any particular moment — even just an hour or two — when you felt genuinely okay or noticed the anxiety had lifted, or has it truly been there every single moment since it started?

No, I really haven't. I mean, I wish I could say there was a time I just... forgot about it for a bit and felt okay, but I haven't. It's just always there. Even if I'm busy, it's like this weight that never actually lifts. So, no, there hasn't been a moment where I felt genuinely okay since all this started.

Has anything happened with the foreclosure situation itself — like maybe you've made a payment plan with the bank, or gotten some legal help, or had any development that gave you even a little bit of hope — and if so, did that actually make your anxiety feel any better?

No, nothing like that has happened. The foreclosure process still isn't resolved at all. I haven't been able to make a payment plan, and I'm still just dealing with the deadlines and the calls from the bank. So, since the situation is still ongoing, the anxiety hasn't let up. It hasn't stopped because the problem hasn't ended.

I know you said the anxiety hasn't really lifted, but I want to make sure I'm understanding correctly — has there been even a single day in these four months where you woke up and the anxiety was completely gone, even if just for that one day?
No, honestly, there hasn't been a single day. I wake up, and it's the first thing I feel. It's just... it's just there, every morning. There hasn't been a day where it was completely gone.

When you're at work focused on a repair job, or doing something that really requires your full concentration, does the anxiety actually feel less intense in those moments, or does it stay just as strong even when you're completely focused on something else?

I'm not really sure if it's less intense, honestly. I haven't really noticed. I mean, when I'm working on a heavy rig or trying to fix an engine, I have to pay attention so I don't mess up or get hurt. But the worry is still just... sitting right there in the back of my mind. I couldn't tell you if it's actually weaker right in those exact moments. I just know it never leaves.
